topic.title: How much a gas station with a store really makes on the gas you buy, and where its profit really comes from

title: At gas stations with a shop, gas is 65% of sales. What's their cut? ⛽
description:
You fill up the tank, so a gas station with a shop gets rich on gas, right? Here's where its money really comes from.
Sources: NACS State of the Industry, NACS/NielsenIQ TDLinx store count (Jan 2026). The characters are not advisers.
Illustrative only. Not financial advice.
cta: Next time you fill up: coffee or no coffee? Comment

lines.text: At gas stations with a shop, gas is 65% of sales. Their cut?
Rohan taps his card, and the card company takes about $140,155 a year from the average store.
So where's the money? Rohan walks in for a coffee and some chips.
The average store sells about $2.2M a year inside the shop.
But the pumps sell the most, so they must keep the most. They don't.
Gas brings only 38.8% of the gross profit. Most of it comes from inside the store.
Coffee or gas: which one is it really selling you? Because

All 5 facts confirmed on the NACS release (15 Apr 2026, latest): 65.0% of sales dollars, 38.8% of gross profit dollars, $341.2B in-store sales, record $21.3B card fees, 151,975 stores (NACS/NIQ TDLinx). The failures are wording.

Beat 'till': 'sells about $2.2M a year in drinks and snacks' is wrong. $341.2B is ALL foodservice and merchandise sales (tobacco, beer, lottery-adjacent goods etc.); foodservice is 28.5% and packaged beverages 18.7% of it. Say 'in coffee, food and everything else in the shop' / 'inside the store'.

Topic verify item 1 not met: title ('Gas is {fact1} of a gas station's sales') and hook ('Gas is 65% of a gas station's sales') must say 'a gas station with a store' or 'a convenience store'. NACS covers convenience stores; only 122,620 of 151,975 sell fuel.

Topic verify item 2 not met: beat 'payoff' says '38.8% of the station's profit'; the source is GROSS profit dollars. Say 'of its gross profit' (and the pylon on-screen label to match if it says profit).
Minor (fix with the above): beat 'fees' 'from every store' and 'till' 'each store like this' are averages over all 151,975 convenience stores; say 'on average' / 'the average store'.
